search.algorithm: deterministic event beam, exact transitions and same-state HP dominance
search.stoppingReason: retained frontier exhausted; earlier beam pruning prevents completeness

finiteResourceCertificate.rankArgument: Always 0<=money<=B. Consumption decreases N-popcount by1 and can raise money by at most B; shop purchase lowers money by25. Thus every retained transition strictly lowers a nonnegative integer rank. Walking/stairs are contracted.

scope.objective: Maximum HP on return to MT1 after the fixed M6 MT2 arrival; any finite sequence in restricted floors 1..3
scope.allowed: Ordinary enemies, doors 2/3/4, items 6..12 and 71, stairs within floors1..3, gold shop1 choices1..3
scope.excluded: Plot/NPC/iron-door events, book UI, other shops, save/load, restart, real clock, other RNG consumption, alternate opening prefixes

search.upperBoundArgument: Current HP + all unconsumed HP potions + 800*floor((current gold + gold of all unconsumed ordinary enemies)/25). All damage is nonnegative, each resource event is once-only, only shop1 HP purchases raise HP otherwise. Ignore reachability, gates and all damage; no attack/defense spending. An upper bound for this restricted continuation only.
search.finitenessArgument: Each consumed tile strictly increases a finite bitmask; between consumptions each successful shop purchase strictly decreases nonnegative integer gold by25. Gold rewards are fixed finite once-only tile rewards. Free walking/stairs/menu identities are contracted. Thus finite resource-changing paths and finite RNG states, with all exact integer resources bounded by finite rewards. This proves the restricted model finite, not whole-game finiteness.

independentGridRouteOracle.independence: Per-floor tile BFS + frame-level ordinary combat; no beam/event-region/dominance/battle-shortcut imports. Uses separately tested shop model and RNG output mixer. Not an exhaustive optimality oracle.

observerFreeControl.settlePolicy: same input order; each recorded nonzero gap padded to max(100ms,gap)+100ms

boundInterval.meaning: Restricted fixed-prefix, fixed-seed continuation only. Lower bound now witnessed by original whole-movie replay; upper bound is a resource relaxation. No completeness or global optimality claim.
